brief: Daily GS TMT sales roundup, not a single-thesis note. Micron beat Q4 revenue ($54.23bn) and EPS ($33.42) and guided Q1 above consensus ($61.5bn revenue, ~$38.15 EPS); AI/HBM demand outstripping supply, with most 2027 HBM capacity already contracted, gives better visibility that the desk reads as positive for memory and WFE names (SK Hynix, Samsung, Lam Research, Applied Materials, ASML, Tokyo Electron, Advantest), while shifting risk toward future capex, valuation and AI-return scrutiny rather than near-term demand. Shares were flat after hours on already-high expectations. Infineon Taiwan MD says AI datacenter power demand (rising rack density, 800V architectures, SiC/GaN content) is causing structural power-semiconductor tightness that normalizes only in 2-3 years, prompting Taiwanese price hikes. On rates, yields rose despite a softer PCE print and Fed Williams comments; GIR pushed its Fed hike call from October to December, and GS own core PCE forecast (3.0% Q4/Q4) sits below the FOMC median (3.4%), implying an October hike is unlikely. Also reported without an argued chain: Tencent ~$7bn Oracle AI-chip lease, Google Gemini 4 Argon launch, Accenture earnings preview, and GS stock calls on Scout24 and Omnicom.
